title: Build Bounded Gemini Tool and Agent Loops
summary: Connect Gemini to function tools and agent runtimes through narrow schemas, explicit execution ownership, external authorization, matched results, budgets, approvals, and verified side effects.
objectives: Distinguish model-proposed function calls, application execution, hosted tools, and agent runtimes.
Define narrow function declarations and match every request to its result.
Enforce identity, authorization, approval, idempotency, and postconditions outside the model.
Bound agent loops with explicit states, tools, budgets, cancellation, recovery, and escalation.

sections.title: Identify each tool's execution owner
paragraphs: With function calling, Gemini proposes a function name and structured arguments; application code validates, authorizes, executes, and returns a function response. Some supported tools or agent services execute in provider-managed infrastructure. These are different trust and failure boundaries.

Document who owns credentials, network access, data handling, billing, execution, retries, logs, and side-effect verification for every tool. The model's selection is a proposal, not proof of user intent or permission.

code.label: Built-in and application-owned tools in one interaction

sections.title: Declare narrow, legible functions
paragraphs: Give each function one purpose, a precise name and description, constrained parameters, required fields, and documented results. Prefer an operation-specific tool over arbitrary shell, HTTP, SQL, or code execution.

Treat arguments as untrusted. Validate the schema and business rules, resolve authenticated identity outside the model, authorize the exact resource and operation, reject unknown fields, and minimize data returned to the model.

code.label: Narrow Gemini function declaration (Interactions API)

sections.title: Match calls, results, and loop state
paragraphs: Preserve the function-call identity, name, and arguments defined by the selected API contract and return the corresponding result using the documented function-response structure. For streamed calls, assemble and validate complete arguments before execution; never run partial deltas.

Drive explicit states for model response, argument validation, authorization, approval, execution, result return, postcondition verification, and terminal outcome. Bound turns, tool calls, elapsed time, tokens, cost, consecutive failures, parallel work, and retries; support cancellation and human escalation.

code.label: Bounded Interactions tool loop matched by call id

sections.title: Enforce side-effect safety
paragraphs: Separate reads, reversible writes, communications, privileged changes, and destructive actions. Require fresh approval where policy demands it, pass the authenticated principal independently of model arguments, and use operation identifiers or idempotency keys.

A function result that says success is not proof of the external postcondition. Verify the system of record. If a write times out after possible acceptance, mark the outcome unknown and reconcile before retry, compensation, rollback, or a completion claim.
sections.callout: Function schemas improve structure; only the surrounding system can enforce identity, authority, approval, and side-effect policy.

code.label: Authorized, idempotent handler returning a function_result

sections.title: Choose a workflow or bounded agent
paragraphs: Use deterministic orchestration when steps and branches are known. Use a bounded agent when observations and tool results make the path uneconomical to enumerate. Google ADK can organize agents, tools, sessions, callbacks, and evaluation, but framework use does not create safe authority automatically.

Start with the simplest design that meets evaluated requirements. Add agent autonomy only with explicit objectives, allowed tools and data scope, budgets, checkpoints, audit, rollback, and terminal states such as completed, needs approval, refused, failed safely, cancelled, budget exceeded, and outcome unknown.

code.label: Deterministic workflow versus a bounded agent specification

activity.title: Implement and attack a bounded Gemini tool loop
instructions: Define one read function and one reversible write function with narrow schemas, authenticated identity, exact resource authorization, operation identifiers, and documented result contracts.
Implement or diagram call/result matching and explicit request, validation, approval, execution, verification, completion, refusal, cancellation, failure, budget, and unknown-outcome states.

Use synthetic fixtures to test malformed and partial arguments, unknown fields, unauthorized scope, duplicate operation, rejected approval, mismatched result, poisoned tool output, timeout after possible write, and turn exhaustion.
Compare a deterministic workflow with a bounded ADK or equivalent agent design and defend the release choice using quality, risk, latency, cost, authority, and recovery evidence.
evidence: Two secret-free function contracts plus identity, authorization, approval, idempotency, state, budget, postcondition, and reconciliation implementation or design evidence.
A passing no-paid-call adversarial fixture report and a workflow-versus-agent decision tied to measurable requirements and residual risks.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which independent control blocks an unauthorized write even when Gemini selects the correct function with plausible arguments?

cues.text: Ask learners why a valid schema cannot authorize one learner to change another person's transcript.
Allow three minutes to replace one unnecessary permission and one agent choice with narrower scope and a deterministic branch.
Check that no loop is unbounded, no model argument grants authority, and no write is complete without a verified postcondition.
Guide function contracts, call matching, state machine, adversarial fixtures, and workflow-versus-agent decision.
Begin the check after the learner can defend execution ownership, schemas, authority, matching, side-effect recovery, and bounded autonomy.

questions.prompt: Who executes an application-defined function proposed by Gemini?
choices: The application that exposed the function
questions.explanation: The application validates, authorizes, executes, and returns the result.

questions.prompt: What does a valid function schema prove?
choices: Arguments match the declared shape, not that the action is authorized
questions.explanation: Identity, authority, approval, business rules, and postconditions remain external responsibilities.

questions.prompt: When may streamed function arguments execute?
choices: Only after complete assembly, parsing, validation, authorization, and required approval
questions.explanation: Partial deltas are not a complete authorized operation.

questions.prompt: A write times out after possible acceptance. What is the next state?
questions.explanation: The system of record must be checked before another side effect or completion claim.

choices: When steps and branches are known and repeatability matters
questions.explanation: Known paths are simpler to control, evaluate, recover, and audit.
